insights.claim: llm-d-router uses a plugin-based architecture with four processing phases (request control, data production, data layer, parsing) driven by an EndpointPickerConfig CRD, enabling runtime-configurable scheduling without redeployment.
insights.reasoning: The analyzer identifies the EPP as a gRPC service with EndpointPickerConfig-driven scheduling, flow control, data-layer, and parsing plugins. This plugin architecture allows operators to tune routing behavior at runtime through CRD configuration rather than code changes.

insights.claim: The component ships three distinct binaries (epp, coordinator, pd-sidecar) as separate container images, each operating as a controller-runtime manager but serving different deployment roles within the llm-d inference stack.
insights.reasoning: The analyzer identifies three Go controller-runtime operators with separate Dockerfiles and entrypoints. Each binary serves a distinct role: EPP handles ExtProc routing, coordinator manages multi-EPP orchestration, and pd-sidecar handles per-pod DNS proxy for KV-cache transfers.

insights.claim: No Kubernetes Service manifests are shipped in the repository; Service definitions are delegated to the deploying operator, creating a tight coupling between llm-d-router and its deployment orchestrator.
insights.reasoning: The analyzer found no Service definitions (coverage status: not-verified), and source inspection confirmed only a placeholder Route manifest exists in deploy/. This means the deploying operator must create Service resources, which couples deployment correctness to external configuration.

insights.claim: The gRPC ExtProc and Health services have no application-level authentication interceptors; security relies entirely on transport TLS configuration and upstream Envoy policy.
insights.reasoning: The analyzer records None for authentication on both gRPC services. Source inspection confirms no auth interceptors are added to the gRPC server options. TLS is optional (--secure-serving flag). In production, the Envoy proxy sitting in front of the EPP is expected to enforce authentication, but the EPP itself has no defense-in-depth authentication layer.
